title: Traffic Guard Rotations and KPI Signalbook
summary: Working playbook for short-window staged rollouts focusing on traffic guard rotations, KPI signal thresholds, and a concise decision ledger. Aimed at product ops people running fast betas and early ramp phases where traffic/pattern changes can cascade into infra or model regression events. Not final; contains heuristics and experimental thresholds we want to validate in the next 2 sprints.
objective: Provide a small, actionable runway document that the on-call traffic guard and product ops lead can use to: (1) interpret KPI deltas, (2) rotate traffic and owner shifts predictably, (3) enact predefined fallbacks quickly, and (4) capture decisions for post-mortem and metric calibration.
kpi_metrics:
Primary KPIs (alert if outside band):
- Error-rate (5xx + model errors): baseline 0.2% — alert at >0.8% sustained 5m, critical >2% 1m
- P95 latency (api): baseline 180ms — alert at >400ms sustained 5m
- Token cost/unit: baseline $0.0009/token — flag if >+40% week-over-week
- Feature adoption (new users hitting feature): baseline 1.2% DAU — investigate if <0.6% after launch week
- Quality signal (eval set pass-rate): baseline 94% — degrade alert if <90% across 2 runs
Notes: these are intentionally conservative for early ramp; we'll tighten targets after canary week.
cadence_and_timeline:
Sprint cadence (example):
- Week 0 (canary day): 100 users, manual monitor, ops rotation A on-call
- Week 1 (phased ramp): 1% traffic -> 5% -> 15%; 1 ops rotation change per day at 8am UTC
- Week 2 (scale test): 15% -> 50% if KPIs stable for 72h; enable autoscale bursts; run cost sampler jobs
- Week 3 (full rollout): 100% if SLOs met for 7d, otherwise apply holdback pattern
Decision gates: must pass latency + error + quality checks at each step. If any single critical KPI trips, execute trigger response in Contingency section.
readiness_checklist:
Pre-launch quick checks (tick boxes, owner initials):
- [ ] Canary infra verified (load gen + smoke tests) — owner: infra-eng
- [ ] Model version pinned and validation eval run (seeded prompts) — owner: applied-ml
- [ ] RBAC and audit logging enabled for rollout group — owner: security
- [ ] Observability dashboards scoped (token-level cost, P95, error heatmap, per-route) — owner: observability
- [ ] Communication channels open (launch Slack channel, runbook pinned) — owner: product-ops
- [ ] Customer success alert rules prepared for early beta customers — owner: customer-success
Notes: leave quick links in the runbook (see linked_artifacts). If anything uncertain, delay canary by 24h.
contingency_triggers_and_actions:
Trigger -> Immediate action -> Owner -> Escalation path:
1) Error-rate >2% 1m or >0.8% sustained 5m -> Pause rollout to previous traffic tier; apply model fallback (lighter quant/model variant) -> product-ops lead -> escalate to SRE and applied-ml lead (ping rotation)
2) P95 latency >800ms 1m -> Throttle batch sizes, increase autoscale burst; if persists >10m, rollback traffic by 50% -> infra lead -> escalate to CTO on-call for customer impact
3) Quality signal drop (>5pp) -> Freeze model deploys, enable higher-precision variant, run targeted eval, notify customers on beta channel -> applied-ml -> escalate to product execs
4) Cost spike >+60% WoW -> Apply cost limiter policy (rate-limit heavy routes); open triage to inspect traffic pattern -> finance strand -> escalate to head of product for business decision
Quick play: script names and run commands (ops):
- ./scripts/pause-rollout.sh <route> (ops)
- ./scripts/pin-model-version.sh <model-v> (applied-ml)
- /ops/rollback-traffic --percent 50 (infra)

risk_register:
1) Model regression undetected by automated evals: mitigation = add small random stress eval sets, manual sample checks during canary
2) Traffic pattern (client bot) causes skewed cost: mitigation = rate limit suspicious clients, add bot signature filters
3) Observability blind spot for route-level token costs: mitigation = add token accounting middleware and short retention debug traces for launch week
4) Miscommunication across teams during night windows: mitigation = pre-scheduled handover notes + 1-hour overlap between rotations
Each risk entry: owner and RTO (target response time) appended to event log for postmortem analysis.
